title: Lusin's theorem for ℝ^N-valued Borel maps on a set of finite μ-measure
statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^N (= EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)); no local finiteness is assumed. Let f : ℝ^N → ℝ^N be Borel measurable, let A ⊆ ℝ^N be a Borel set with μ(A) < ∞, and let ε ∈ (0, ∞]. Then there is a closed set C ⊆ ℝ^N with C ⊆ A, μ(A ∖ C) < ε, and f continuous on C (i.e. the restriction f|C is continuous).
lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn N) (A : Set (Rn N)), Measurable f → MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ C ⊆ A, IsClosed C ∧ μ (A \ C) < ε ∧ ContinuousOn f C
